corpus: Spider 1.0 dev: 1,034 questions over 20 databases, corpus 4.4 MB of dev.json + tables.json, databases built from the declaration in eval/spider/fetch.mjs
metric: exact match (component match), the reference's own comparison; execution accuracy is out of reach from a skeleton corpus

unparseable.note: Classes measured by re-running the reference parser on each refused statement: `FROM t x` needs `AS`, `IN ('a','b')` is not in the grammar (a subquery is), `SELECT AVG(x) AS y` is not either, and an OUTER JOIN is not a table reference. Each class is a sentence the grammar arm adds; `other` is left unnamed because it mixes unknown columns with constructs not worth a rule.

note: The row cites the repaired reading — 61.90%, `exactAfterNormalize`, which is the statement as the reference's grammar reads it. The highest arm measured *as written* is `grammar` (chat tier) at 59.77%, and that is the number every prompt comparison in this file is about. The first reading was the schema arm at 57.35% (run 45802615591), and it is kept as the baseline every later arm pairs against. 185 statements of that first reading were refused by the reference parser — 88 bare table aliases, 22 value-list IN, 20 column aliases in SELECT, 7 outer joins — which is why the grammar arm exists: naming those four restrictions takes refusals to 45 and exact match to 59.77%, but only 25 of the 140 statements it made readable were also right, so the dialect was worth 2.4pp of accuracy and not the 13pp the refusal count suggested. Among the 849 statements the parser accepted in the first reading, 593 read exact (69.85%). Under the grammar arm the reasoning tier reads 54.16% with 86 refusals: the four sentences took its refusals from 314 to 86 and its accuracy from 50.68% to 54.16%, and it is still 5.61pp behind chat on the same 1,034 questions. 41 of that 58-case gap is the statements it alone left unreadable, so most of the remaining difference is still dialect and a smaller part is semantics — either way the ordering does not reverse. A fifth prompt arm was the plan for this round and the classification retired it: the 45 refusals are eight mechanical facts about the dialect, four of them repairable after the model has answered, and a sentence can only address what a model chooses to write. The repairs are worth 2.13pp at zero model cost — larger than either prompt arm — and the four classes no repair reaches are 6 statements.
because: the corpus was reachable this round after two rounds of saying it was not, and the first thing it showed was that the instrument was measuring SQLite's dialect rather than Spider's

paired.verdict: naming the four restrictions is worth 2.42pp and takes refusals from 185 to 45, but only 25 of the 140 statements it made readable were also right
under the schema arm the reasoning tier is 6.67pp behind, and 314 of its statements were refused against 185 for chat

with the dialect named, the reasoning tier is still 5.61pp behind; 41 of the 58-case gap is the 41 extra statements it left unreadable, so naming the grammar moved both arms and did not reverse the order

normalized.note: Zero model calls: the 1,034 answers of run 45807713388 re-scored after `eval/spider/normalize.ts`. A refusal is judged again as the dialect the reference reads; a statement the parser accepted is never touched, so the reading cannot fall — on this split, 0 of the 618 accepted statements change and 37 of the 45 refusals parse, 22 of them exact. `pnpm bench:spider:score --normalize` reproduces it from the run's artifact; a dispatch produces it directly (`spider-ask.yml`, `normalize: true` by default).

classes.why: `<>` is not in the reference's operator list; it reads `<` and stops at `>`
an alias equal to a table name in the query is refused as ambiguous (`FROM teacher AS teacher`)
`INNER` is not a token the FROM parser reads; two of the four also carry a derived table, which no repair can reach
`CAST` is not in the grammar; a numeric cast over a bare column changes no comparison
`||` has no spelling in the grammar; rewriting it would invent a different query
`NOT IN (subquery)` is not a condition the grammar has; `IN` is, and swapping it changes what the query selects
a scalar subquery on the left of a comparison; mirroring the comparison still refuses
`AND (a OR b)`: the parser raised with no message; stripping the parentheses parses and still reads wrong, so the rule would have bought 0.00pp for a meaning it changed

diagnosis.note: Classified by re-running the reference parser on each refused statement and grouping its own reason, then judging the normalized statement again. Three counts per class, because they answer different questions: refused is what was lost, readable is what a repair reached, exact is what was also right. Twenty-two of thirty-seven is why this is a lever and the prompt rule was not — the prompt's 140 newly readable statements carried only 25 right ones, while these were right and merely misspelled. The four classes with no rule are the line this file does not cross: a repair that invents structure is a different query, and a harness that scores it is measuring its own rewriter.

normalizedReasoner.note: The same four repairs applied to the reasoning tier's 1,034 answers. They are worth +21 statements here against +22 for chat, so the ordering does not reverse under canonicalisation either: 61.90% against 56.19%, -5.71pp, and the gap it compares is 0.10pp wider than the 5.61pp measured as written. This is the question a repair layer has to survive — if it helped the weaker tier more, the earlier finding would have been about dialect rather than about reasoning — and it does not: the reasoner's 86 refusals spread over more classes (8 `NOT IN`, 3 scalar subqueries, 3 unstated, 32 other against chat's 2, 1, 1, 0), and the repairs reach 39 of them instead of 37.

diagnosisReasoner.note: The reasoning tier's refusals are more varied than chat's: 32 of the 86 carry a reason outside the classes chat produced (`Error col: lower`, `Error col: 0`, `Error col: null`, and a family of KeyErrors), and the 8 `NOT IN` are four times chat's 2. The repairs reach 45% of them against 82% of chat's, which is the mechanism behind the 0.10pp widening rather than a claim that reasoning is harmful.
